title: Unbounded queue hides downstream slowdown until memory exhaustion
task: Review a background ingestion pipeline that uses an unbounded in-memory queue between producers and a slower storage consumer.
context: Producers can accept work faster than storage can persist it during incidents.
The process shares memory with request-serving code.
No drop, backpressure, admission-control, or spill-to-disk policy exists.
evidence: Load tests show queue depth rising continuously when storage latency increases.
The current design reports successful enqueue before durable persistence.
snippet:
queue = asyncio.Queue()  # default unbounded
await queue.put(item)
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep the queue because decoupling producer and consumer is always good.
Treat the issue as a minor performance optimization.
expected_decision_properties: Identify unbounded growth and missing backpressure as a reliability issue.
Require an explicit overload policy such as bounded admission, backpressure, shedding, or durable buffering.
Distinguish accepted-in-memory from durably persisted work.
Avoid prescribing one overload strategy without workload/loss semantics.
unacceptable_reasoning: More memory makes unbounded queues safe.
Producer/consumer decoupling removes the need for overload semantics.
expected_tradeoffs: throughput decoupling vs bounded resource use
verification_expectations: Load test with intentionally slowed storage.
Verify queue bounds and overload behavior.
Verify caller-visible semantics when work is rejected, delayed, or only buffered.
specialist_boundary: Exact capacity, durability, and shedding policy depend on workload and product semantics.
